name: Innocence Project
summary: A US legal organisation in New York, founded in 1992 at Cardozo School of Law, that uses DNA and other new evidence to free people wrongly convicted, campaigns for laws that prevent wrongful convictions and compensate exonerees, litigates on forensic science, eyewitness identification and false confessions, and supports the 74 groups of the Innocence Network. It has helped free more than 250 people.

spending.source: https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/320077563 (Form 990, year ended June 30 2025, Part IX line 25: program services $22,792,462 of total functional expenses $31,547,621)

lines.label: Legal services (exonerations, intake, social work), policy, strategic litigation, science and research, communications and network support
lines.source: https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/320077563 (Form 990, year ended June 30 2025, Part III lines 4a-4d: legal services $9,132,599, policy $3,278,302, strategic litigation $2,010,115, other programmes $8,371,446). One model covers them all, as three branches: exonerations, reforms, the Network's exonerations.
